title: The Book of Obadiah
lead: The shortest book of the Old Testament: twenty-one verses against Edom, the nation descended from Esau, for standing by when Jerusalem fell, followed by the day of the LORD for all nations and a promise of Zion's recovery. Its first nine verses echo Jeremiah 49:7-22.

sections.b: Obadiah has three parts. Verses 1-9 announce Edom's fall from its cliff-top strongholds; verses 10-14 give the reason, Edom's violence against its brother Jacob on the day Jerusalem fell, in eight "do not" lines; verses 15-21 widen to the day of the LORD for all the nations and promise Zion's survivors, a restored map and the LORD's rule. The prophet is named only as "Obadiah," a common name meaning "servant of the LORD." Most scholars date the charge to the years after 586 BC, with a minority preferring the 800s BC. The relation of verses 1-9 to Jeremiah 49:7-22 (borrowing either way, or a common source) is a main question.
